ghs.en: The doorbell called back an awareness that had nearly left for the pleasant comfortableness of the other side.
ghs.assessment: The sequence of comfort, awareness of the world outside, and the doorbell recalling it remains recoverable. The confirmed defect is the tangled, nonidiomatic clause structure rather than a wholesale semantic reversal.
ghs.remedy: State the recovered sequence in grammatical narrative English.

highlights.text: The doorbell called back an awareness that had nearly left for the pleasant comfortableness of the other side.

rows.jp: 「やべ」

ghs.remedy: Use “I put on a kimono and headed to the entryway.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "A gangster-like surname associated with a conversely kyute voice... Yusa-chan? It's open, do come in!"

rows.jp: ドアがおそるおそる開き、美少女が立っていた。

ghs.en: Slowly and carefully the door opens, and there stood a beautiful girl.
ghs.assessment: The English shifts from present “opens” to past “stood” inside one coordinated event, producing an unsupported tense break.
ghs.remedy: Use “The door slowly and carefully opened, and there stood a beautiful girl.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Well, the hair is indeed giving it some white and... it suits you, I think."
ghs.assessment: The English eventually says that the colors suit him, but muddles the source's unfinished explanation that his white hair is why they suit him.

ghs.remedy: Use “A wry smile rose to my face.”

highlights.text: Rise a bitter smile to the surface.

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wouldn't it'd fit you a lot better, Yusa-chan?"
ghs.assessment: “Wouldn’t it’d” combines two incompatible auxiliary constructions. The source asks whether the kimono would suit Yusa better.
ghs.remedy: Use “Wouldn’t it suit you much better, Yusa-chan?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Wouldn't it'd fit you a lot better, Yusa-chan?"

ghs.assessment: The unfinished B-but it's can enact a flustered refusal, so a polarity reversal is not established. The remaining defect is that the fragment is too weak and structurally broken to carry the response cleanly.
ghs.remedy: Use a natural interrupted protest.

highlights.text: Yusa: "B-, but it's... hic!"

ghs.remedy: Keep the exciting-news sense in grammatical English.

highlights.text: Taichi: "So, what thrilling news may you be bringing me bring here on this day?"

rows.jp: 『光源氏は本当にウハウハなのか大検証』というこの企画は、今のところ順調と判断できるデータが揃いつつある。

ghs.assessment: The coined project title asks whether Hikaru Genji was really living it up. The English changes Hikaru to Hikari and reduces the title to an ungrammatical string that does not preserve the question.
ghs.remedy: Use a coherent title such as “The ‘Was Hikaru Genji Really Living It Up?’ Comprehensive Investigation.”

highlights.text: The Super Was Hikari Genji Truly All Satisfied Smiles Experiment, as I call my plan, has presently assembled sufficient data to produce a judgment of 'favorable'.

rows.jp: 成功したあとについてあんまり考えていなかったことには、今気づいた。

ghs.remedy: Use “I only just realized that I hadn’t given much thought to what I would do if it succeeded.”

highlights.text: As to how I hadn't given much thought what to do after a success, I realized it just now.

highlights.text: She rocks back and forth above her lap fingers that don't wish to readily settle down.

rows.en: “By the standards of the physical world, every form of Being may be assigned to one of several models.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "According to materialistic values, each and every one of those 'existences' can be classified into into a number of models. Bowl Type and Rocket Type top the list, while Temple Bell Type, Hang-down Type and Platter Type are also common."

rows.jp: 「『椀型』『ロケット型』などを筆頭に『釣り鐘型』『下垂れ型』『皿型』なども多い。微にいり細を穿つ観点で『先端陥没型』といった例も報告されて……」
rows.en: “The principal models are bowl-shaped and rocket-shaped; then come bell-shaped, pendulous, and saucer-shaped. A truly exacting taxonomy must also account for documented cases of the inverted-nipple type...”

rows.jp: ふと遊紗ちゃんを見ると、メモっていた。
rows.en: I glanced at Yusa. She was taking notes.

ghs.en: Casually my glance fell on Yusa-chan, and she was taking notes.

rows.jp: 「うわあああああっ、だめ、ダメェ～っ！！？？」
rows.en: “Nooooo! Stop! Stooop!!??”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Bwaaaaaah! You can't, you CAAA～N'T!?!?!?"

rows.jp: 「え、どうしましたですっ？」
rows.en: “Huh? What happened?!”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Eh? What is wrong with that?"
ghs.assessment: Yusa asks what is wrong or what happened. “With that” invents a specific object of objection and makes her defend the note-taking.
ghs.remedy: Use “Huh? What’s wrong?”

highlights.text: Yusa: "Eh? What is wrong with that?"

rows.jp: 「記録してはいけないのっ」
rows.en: “You mustn’t write this down!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Making recordings is out of the question!"
ghs.assessment: In context he forbids writing the information down. “Making recordings” commonly means audio or video recording and obscures the written-note action shown by the source.
ghs.remedy: Use “You mustn’t write that down!”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Making recordings is out of the question!"

rows.jp: 「あ、あんまり難しかったので、あとで調べようと思ったですが……？」
rows.en: “I-it was so difficult, I thought I’d look it up later...?”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Ah, but the words are kind of difficult, so I was thinking I'd look them up later...?"

rows.jp: なんですとぅ！？
rows.en: She was going to what?!

ghs.en: WHAAAT'd she SAAAY?!

rows.jp: 今のデンジャラスワードをインターネットなどでリサーチされたりしたら！！
rows.en: If she searched those dangerous words on the internet...!

ghs.en: She wants to implement the act of Research on these Dangerous Words on the Internet etc.!!!
ghs.assessment: The source fears what would happen if she researched the dangerous words online. The English turns the hypothetical fear into her present desire and renders it as bureaucratic nonsense.
ghs.remedy: Use “If she researched those dangerous words on the internet...!”

highlights.text: She wants to implement the act of Research on these Dangerous Words on the Internet etc.!!!

rows.jp: 「危ない！　伏せろ！」
rows.en: “Danger! Get down!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Watch out! Ambush!"
ghs.assessment: 伏せろ is the command “Get down!” The English replaces the command with the noun “Ambush!”
ghs.remedy: Use “Watch out! Get down!”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Watch out! Ambush!"

rows.jp: 抱き寄せて、電柱の陰に隠れる。
rows.en: I pulled her close and took cover behind a utility pole.

ghs.en: I embrace her, and we hide behind an utility pole.
ghs.assessment: The indefinite article before “utility” must be “a,” not “an,” because the word begins with a consonant sound.
ghs.remedy: Use “We duck behind a utility pole.”

highlights.text: I embrace her, and we hide behind an utility pole.

rows.jp: 「はらーっ！？」
rows.en: “Whaaat!?”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Bwha--?!"

rows.jp: 「静かにしろここは戦場だ」
rows.en: “Quiet. This is a battlefield.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Quiet and be still, this is a battlefield."

rows.jp: 「平和な日本の街並みにしか見えないここが、戦場っ！？」
rows.en: “This peaceful Japanese street is a battlefield!?”

ghs.en: Yusa: "This place I can't see as anything but a peaceful townscape of Japan is now a battlefield?!"

rows.jp: 「うむ。今、ソルジャー兵士の殺気を感じた」
rows.en: “Indeed. I just sensed the killing intent of a soldier-trooper.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "So it is! Just now I felt the blood thirst of a Heishi Soldier!"

rows.jp: 「そるじゃー兵士！？」
rows.en: “A soldier-trooper!?”

ghs.en: Yusa: "But then, it's a soldier?!?"
ghs.assessment: The source incredulously repeats the intentionally redundant hybrid “soldier-soldier.” The English removes that repetition and asks only whether it is a soldier.
ghs.remedy: Preserve the bilingual redundancy: “A ‘soldier soldier’!?”

highlights.text: Yusa: "But then, it's a soldier?!?"

rows.jp: 「ＣＩＡかＫＧＢ、あるいはＮ○Ｋという可能性もある」
rows.en: “It may be the CIA, the KGB, or possibly N○K.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "From the CIA or the KGB, but there is the possibility of the N*K as well."
ghs.assessment: The source lists CIA, KGB, or possibly N*K as alternatives. “From ... but there is” does not form a grammatical alternative list.
ghs.remedy: Use “It might be the CIA, the KGB, or even N*K.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "From the CIA or the KGB, but there is the possibility of the N*K as well."

rows.jp: 「どれも極めて武力的な諜報機関だ」
rows.en: “All three are exceptionally militant intelligence agencies.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Any of them is an extraordinarily militarized intelligence agency."

rows.jp: 「特に最後のグループは、極めて凶悪で、民家を急襲して現金を強奪していくというゲリラ的凶行に及ぶことで知られている」
rows.en: “The last is particularly vicious. It is infamous for guerrilla raids on private homes, where its agents seize cash from the residents.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That last group, in particular, is of a brutality so extreme that it is known for guerrilla-like violence, resorting even to assaulting private homes and pillaging cash."

rows.jp: 「ひぇぇぇ」
rows.en: “Eeeeeek...”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Hyyy!"

rows.jp: 「……行ったか。よし、もういいだろう」
rows.en: “...They’re gone. Good. It should be safe now.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...he's gone. Good, we should be safe now."

rows.jp: 道に戻る。
rows.en: We returned to the road.

ghs.en: Back to the street.

rows.jp: たまたま通りかかった帰宅中のサラリーマンが、怪訝な顔でこちらを見ていた。
rows.en: An office worker on his way home passed by and gave us a puzzled look.

ghs.en: That salaryman on his way home that we accidentally happened to pass looked at us with doubt on his face.
ghs.assessment: “Accidentally happened” redundantly marks chance twice, and the source describes a puzzled or suspicious look rather than abstract “doubt on his face.”
ghs.remedy: Use “A salaryman who happened to be passing on his way home gave us a puzzled look.”

highlights.text: That salaryman on his way home that we accidentally happened to pass looked at us with doubt on his face.

rows.jp: どこからかナイターの中継なども聞こえてきたりして、牧歌的な夜道であった。
rows.en: A baseball broadcast drifted from somewhere nearby. It was an idyllic night.

ghs.en: An idyllic journey at night, where one could even hear the relay broadcast of the night's game from somewhere.

rows.jp: 「すまないね。そんなわけで、君に話した内容は機密情報なんだ。記録すると君の清純ボディが危ない」
rows.en: “Forgive me. As you can see, everything I told you is classified. If you record it, your pure and innocent body will be in danger.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "My apologies. As you saw, the subjects I discussed are confidential information. Recording them would be perilous to your innocent body."

rows.jp: 「な、なんと」
rows.en: “G-goodness.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Wo-, whoa."

rows.jp: 「すまないが、該当する部分を削除してはもらえまいか？」
rows.en: “I’m afraid I must ask you to delete the relevant passage.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "My apologies, but may I ask you to erase the relevant parts?"

rows.jp: 「は、はい、消します、ごめんなさいっ」
rows.en: “Y-yes. I’ll erase it. I’m sorry!”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Y-, yes, I will erase, I'm sorry!"

rows.jp: シャーペンの背についてる消しゴムで、こすこすと紙面にリセットをかける。
rows.en: With the eraser on the end of her mechanical pencil, she rubbed the page back to its factory settings.

ghs.en: And with the eraser attached to the back of the pencil, scrub scrub the page is reset.
ghs.assessment: The local agent is Yusa, who is erasing her notes. The original wrong-subject charge was itself wrong; the surviving defect is the omission of that recoverable agent and the mixed, ungrammatical clauses.
ghs.remedy: State naturally that Yusa erased her notes and reset them.

highlights.text: And with the eraser attached to the back of the pencil, scrub scrub the page is reset.

rows.jp: ああ、汚れのないその消しゴム、使わずにとっておいたのだろうに……。
rows.en: Ah, that pristine eraser. She must have been saving it, untouched...

ghs.en: Ahhh, that eraser so unsullied, likely kept in reserve unused...

rows.jp: 「申し訳ない」
rows.en: “My apologies.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "My deepest apologies."

rows.jp: 「いいんです。わたしが悪いんです」
rows.en: “It’s all right. It was my fault.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "It is all right! It is my bad!"
ghs.assessment: My bad is valid US English, but It is my bad is awkward and much too casual for this speaker's register.
ghs.remedy: Use It's my fault in the speaker's established register.

highlights.text: Yusa: "It is all right! It is my bad!"

rows.jp: 胸が痛かった。
rows.en: My heart hurt.

ghs.en: My heart was in pain.

rows.jp: というか、俺が痛かった。
rows.en: No—the painful thing here was me.

ghs.en: Or should I say, I was in pain.
